title: Task-oriented data table controls
summary: Add sorting, filtering, column choices, row actions, and density controls only when they support real user tasks, with current state visible and reversible.
problem: Generated admin tables often accumulate every possible control while hiding which constraints or sort states are active.
use_when: Users repeatedly inspect or act on structured data
The dataset is large enough that control over ordering or visibility saves meaningful time
avoid_when: The table is small and read-only and extra controls add more complexity than value
rationale: Data tools should reflect jobs users perform, not a checklist of table features.
State visibility is essential when controls change what rows are shown.

use_if: Users repeatedly inspect or act on structured data
The dataset is large enough that control over ordering or visibility saves meaningful time
prefer_alternatives_if: A simpler list or static table supports the task

requirements: Label sort and filter state programmatically.
Keep row actions discoverable without hover-only controls.
Preserve usable reading order under responsive transformations.
Start from user tasks before adding controls.
Show active sort and filter state.
Keep row actions near the affected row and avoid ambiguous icon-only actions.
